text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Spanish embassy resumes activities in Baghdad
- Newspapers in the Arab world laud Iraq's steadfastness in the face of the crime of the embargo.
- Cuban President Fidel Castro says the United States is turning into a dustbin empire.
- British MP denounces U.S. Secretary of State Madeline Albright for anti-Iraq attitudes.
- U.N. General Assembly defeats Washington and adopts resolution denouncing Israeli housing activities in Jerusalem.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ and JUMHOURIYA)
- Article on how ethics of war were applied during the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
- Article details the heroic feats of President Saddam Hussein.
- Iraq's Chamber of Industries embarks on an extensive survey of industrial projects in Iraq.
- Oil Ministry source says Iraq facing no problems with international overseers supervising partial exports under a deal with U.N.
- An open letter advises U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan on what to do to control U.N. agencies.
- Commentary denounces British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rikind.
- Article on the economic returns of a new law which forces tenants of commercial property to pay an economic price to owners.
